headline: Argentine Sovereign Bonds Fall 2% as Country Risk Rises to 1,094 Basis Points
summary: Argentine Global bonds fell 2% and JP Morgan's country risk index rose 62 units to 1,094 basis points. Local assets were dragged down by profit-taking and selling pressure across Wall Street markets.
why: JP Morgan's EMBI index measures the sovereign risk spread of emerging market bonds over US Treasuries.

impacts.name: Argentina
impacts.why: Global bond prices fell 2% and country risk rose to 1,094 basis points.
